Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

adjudication_records.issue_text: backupCode field is missing from formSchema, so zodResolver strips it from LoginValues and signIn('credentials') submits without it, making backup-code login non-functional

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `LoginValues` gains `backupCode` and `BackupCode` registers `methods.register("backupCode")`, but it does not show the definition of `formSchema` used by `zodResolver(formSchema)` in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`. Since `formSchema` is not included/modified in this diff, the claim that it is missing `backupCode` (and that zod strips it, breaking submission) cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is set to null and persisted immediately after matching in authorize, but downstream checks can still throw, burning single-use codes without granting a session

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` the code immediately nulls the matched backup code and persists it via `await prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } })` after a match. This consumption happens inside `authorize` before the sign-in flow is fully completed (i.e., before the overall auth process is guaranteed to succeed). If anything after this point fails (in remaining `authorize` logic not shown here, or in downstream NextAuth session/token creation), the backup code would already be burned without a successful login/session.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Enable-flow Cancel button is hidden on the DisplayBackupCodes step and onOpenChange is not guarded, so backdrop/Esc dismissal closes the modal without calling onEnable or resetting state, permanently losing displayed backup codes

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, after `handleEnable` succeeds it does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` instead of calling `onEnable()` (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx). On that `DisplayBackupCodes` step, the Cancel button is explicitly not rendered (`{step !== SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes ? <Button ...>{t("cancel")}</Button> : null}`), but the modal can still be closed via `Dialog` backdrop/Esc because `onOpenChange` is passed through unconditionally and no handler resets state or calls `onEnable` when `open` becomes false. That means a user can dismiss the modal without triggering the `backup-codes-close` path that calls `resetState(); onEnable();`, potentially leaving the parent unaware that 2FA is enabled and losing the only UI opportunity to copy/download the displayed backup codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resetState never revokes the backupCodesUrl object URL on cancel/close or unmount, leaking blob URLs across enable/cancel cycles
resetForm in DisableTwoFactorModal doesn't reset the 2fa1-2fa6 digit fields, leaving stale TOTP digits that can repopulate a code the user can't see, causing confusing 'incorrect 2fa' rejections

adjudication.rationale: In DisableTwoFactorModal, `resetForm` explicitly clears `totpCode` via `form.setValue("totpCode", "")`. The PR diff does not show that the per-digit inputs (`2fa1`–`2fa6`) are registered into this modal’s react-hook-form state or that they can repopulate `totpCode` after being cleared. Also, when switching to backup-code flow, `<TwoFactor />` is unmounted (replaced by `<BackupCode />`), which would clear any local digit state inside `TwoFactor`. So the claimed stale hidden digits causing incorrect rejections isn’t verifiable from the shown diff.

matched_golden_ids: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying issue: backup code validation/matching is case-sensitive (e.g., using indexOf / comparing against lowercase hex) without normalization, causing uppercase hex input to be rejected, whereas codes should be treated case-insensitively for better UX.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes) state is inferred as never[] and lacks runtime validation of body.backupCodes, risking a render crash on non-array responses

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);` leaves `backupCodes` inferred as `never[]` (no explicit `string[]`), reducing type safety. Additionally, `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` assigns unvalidated JSON to state, and the UI later does `backupCodes.map(...)` (and `backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode)`), which would throw at render-time if `body.backupCodes` is not an array (e.g., unexpected API response shape). This is a robustness/type-safety concern rather than a guaranteed runtime defect given the same PR’s API returns `backupCodes` as an array on 200 responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: E2e coverage gap: login-with-backup-code and disable-with-backup-code paths are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new backup-code authentication paths (login via `credentials.backupCode` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, and disabling 2FA via `req.body.backupCode` in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, plus new UI toggles in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` and `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx`). The only e2e changes in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` add tests around backup-code display/download/copy/close after enabling 2FA, and even include a TODO explicitly noting missing tests for "login + disabling 2fa with backup". There is no e2e test exercising logging in with a backup code or disabling 2FA using a backup code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are compared with indexOf (non-constant-time comparison) in next-auth-options.ts:147 and disable.ts:60, deviating from constant-time 2FA hygiene

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show backup code verification using `indexOf(...)` over decrypted codes in both `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (around the new backup-code login branch) and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (backup-code disable branch). This is a variable-time lookup/compare pattern (string comparisons and early-exit search) and could be tightened to constant-time comparisons for 2FA-related secrets. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove an exploitable vulnerability or broken behavior (no evidence of missing rate limits, remote timing exposure feasibility, etc.), so it’s better treated as a security hardening concern rather than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race in single-use backup code enforcement: read-then-write pattern in next-auth-options.ts:150-159 allows the same code to be consumed twice under concurrent logins
Backup code is consumed (side effect in authorize) before login is guaranteed to succeed, so later failures still burn the code

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` inside `authorize`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` the code immediately marks the backup code as used (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and persists it via `prisma.user.update(...)` before the overall sign-in flow is complete/confirmed. Since `authorize` returning successfully is only one step in the NextAuth login process, any subsequent failure (later logic in `authorize` not shown here, or downstream NextAuth callbacks/session issuance) would still leave the backup code consumed even though the user is not logged in.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are generated and persisted at setup stage before 2FA is actually enabled, leaving unused codes in DB and silently invalidating earlier codes on re-setup

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup call generates `backupCodes` and immediately persists them to the user record (`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...)`) even though `twoFactorEnabled` is explicitly set to `false` at setup time. This means codes can be stored even if the user cancels before enabling 2FA, and repeated setup calls will overwrite the stored `backupCodes` with a new set. The diff doesn’t show this causing an immediate functional failure (backup codes are only accepted when `twoFactorEnabled` is true), but it is a real, diff-grounded lifecycle/UX/security hygiene concern: unused codes can linger, and prior generated codes become invalid on re-setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled JSON.parse on decrypted backup codes in disable.ts:57 and next-auth-options.ts:139 can throw and cause a 500 on corrupted ciphertext or rotated encryption key

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` for `user.backupCodes` in both `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (new backup-code branch) and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (authorize backupCode flow) without any try/catch or validation. If ciphertext is corrupted, `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is rotated/mismatched, or decrypted plaintext is not valid JSON, `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and/or `JSON.parse(...)` can throw and bubble up (API route / next-auth authorize), producing an unhandled exception and likely a 500 rather than a controlled auth error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message for missing_backup_codes tells users to generate codes in settings but no standalone regeneration feature exists; disabling and re-enabling 2FA silently invalidates all saved backup codes with no path to regenerate

adjudication.rationale: The locale string for `missing_backup_codes` says “Please generate them in your settings.” (apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json), but the diff only generates backup codes during 2FA setup (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` returns `backupCodes` and EnableTwoFactorModal displays them). There is no explicit “regenerate backup codes” action in settings shown in this diff; users missing codes (e.g., existing 2FA users with `backupCodes: null`) would not have a direct regeneration path besides disabling/re-enabling 2FA. Also, disabling 2FA clears `backupCodes` (`disable.ts` sets `backupCodes: null`), so any previously saved codes become unusable without a clear UX explanation. This is a product/UX gap rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code consumption in login is not atomic (read-modify-write race in next-auth-options.ts) allowing a single-use code to be replayed by concurrent logins
matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe a race condition where backup code validation/consumption is done via a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing two concurrent logins using the same backup code to both pass and effectively reuse a one-time code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are regenerated and overwritten on every /setup call before 2FA enablement is confirmed, silently invalidating previously issued codes

adjudication.rationale: In `/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, every setup call generates a fresh `backupCodes` array (`crypto.randomBytes...`) and immediately persists it to the user record (`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...)`) alongside resetting `twoFactorEnabled: false` and updating `twoFactorSecret`. This happens before 2FA enablement is confirmed (enable is a later step), so repeated or abandoned setup attempts will overwrite any previously stored backup codes (and secret) without confirmation, effectively invalidating previously issued codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code comparison uses Array.prototype.indexOf instead of constant-time comparison, creating a timing oracle in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts

adjudication.rationale: Both in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the user-supplied backup code is checked via `backupCodes.indexOf(<input>)`. This relies on normal JS string equality during `indexOf`, which is not constant-time and also exits early based on where (or whether) a match occurs, so response time can vary with the secret value/position. That is a real security defect (timing side-channel) in the newly introduced backup-code verification path.

matched_golden_ids: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the object URL for backup codes (backupCodesUrl) is never revoked on close/unmount, causing a blob/object URL memory leak. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about not revoking the object URL on component unmount leading to increased memory usage over time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: onEnable callback contract broken: 2FA is enabled server-side but parent's onEnable never runs if dialog dismissed via onOpenChange/X, causing silent state divergence

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, after the enable API returns 200, the code no longer calls `onEnable()` and instead moves to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` (`handleEnable`: `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)`). In that step, the cancel button is removed and `onEnable()` is only invoked by the explicit “close” button handler (`backup-codes-close`). The modal does not handle `onOpenChange` to call `onEnable()` or `resetState()`. Therefore, if the dialog is dismissed via the dialog’s close affordance (X/overlay) triggering `onOpenChange` rather than the “close” button, the server-side state may be enabled while the parent never receives `onEnable()`, and the modal state may also remain at `DisplayBackupCodes` on next open.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes shown exactly once with no regeneration endpoint while 2FA is enabled; losing TOTP plus unsaved codes leads to permanent lockout

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup codes are generated once during `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` and stored encrypted on the user (`backupCodes`), then only displayed in `EnableTwoFactorModal` at the new `DisplayBackupCodes` step with copy/download/close actions. There is no regeneration/re-display flow added in this diff (no endpoint or UI in settings to fetch/regenerate codes while 2FA remains enabled). Because login/disable rely on either TOTP or a backup code, a user who enables 2FA, closes the backup-code step without saving, and later loses TOTP would be unable to authenticate (the diff does not show any recovery path). This is a scope/UX/edge-case concern grounded in the added flows, not a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setup.ts uses CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY without a missing/undefined guard, unlike disable.ts and next-auth-options.ts

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the handler encrypts both `backupCodes` and `twoFactorSecret` via `symmetricEncrypt(..., process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` with no check that `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set. In contrast, `disable.ts` and `next-auth-options.ts` explicitly guard against a missing key before decrypting/encrypting backup codes. If the env var is undefined, setup can throw or behave incorrectly when generating/encrypting backup codes (and secret).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disable endpoint doesn't consume the used backup code at verification time, creating inconsistent consumption semantics vs login path; errors between verification and update leave a verified code valid

adjudication.rationale: In `/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the backup-code branch verifies a matching code (`indexOf(...)`) but does not remove/consume it at verification time; it relies on the final `prisma.user.update` to clear `backupCodes: null` only upon successful disable. That is inconsistent with the login path in `next-auth-options.ts`, which consumes a single used backup code immediately by re-encrypting the updated list. The finding’s point about failures between verification and the final update leaving the verified code reusable is plausible (e.g., DB/update error), but it’s an edge-case/semantic inconsistency rather than a clearly broken behavior because a successful disable clears all codes anyway.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:92 calls body.backupCodes.map(...) unguarded, causing TypeError if backupCodes is undefined (old API or older cached bundle)

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.handleSetup, on `response.status === 200` it uses `body.backupCodes.map(...)` to build the Blob URL without validating `body.backupCodes` is an array. In this PR’s server diff, `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` now returns `{..., backupCodes}`, so in the matched-version happy path it won’t be undefined; however the frontend code is not defensive against a 200 response missing that field (e.g., mismatched/rolling deploy), which would throw a TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: URL.createObjectURL leaks on unmount since object URL is only revoked when a new one is created

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, an object URL is created via `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` and stored in `backupCodesUrl` (setup handler). The code only calls `URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl)` when generating a *new* URL (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), but there is no cleanup on modal close/cancel (`resetState()` doesn’t revoke or clear `backupCodesUrl`) and no `useEffect` cleanup on unmount. This can leak the object URL for the lifetime of the page/session if the component unmounts or the modal is closed without creating a new URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code comparison uses Array.indexOf (non-constant-time) at auth boundary, inconsistent with rest of 2FA flow

adjudication.rationale: The diff does compare user-supplied backup codes via linear search with `Array.indexOf(...)` in two auth-adjacent paths: `disable.ts` (`const index = backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));`) and `next-auth-options.ts` (`const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));`). That is not a constant-time comparison and could be considered a security-hardening issue at an authentication boundary. However, the diff doesn’t show what the “rest of 2FA flow” does internally (e.g., whether TOTP checks are constant-time), so the “inconsistent with rest” part isn’t fully verifiable, and this is more best-practice than a demonstrable functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: formSchema not updated to include backupCode, so zodResolver strips the field and signIn receives undefined backupCode, deadening the backup-code login path

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `LoginValues` gaining `backupCode` and `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })`, but it does not show the definition of `formSchema` or whether it was updated elsewhere. Without seeing `formSchema`, we can’t verify the claim that the zod resolver strips `backupCode` and that `signIn` receives it as `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code verification check and consumption are non-atomic (TOCTOU race), allowing a single-use code to grant two concurrent sessions; same pattern in disable endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login does a non-atomic read/modify/write: it decrypts `user.backupCodes`, checks `index = backupCodes.indexOf(...)`, then later updates with `backupCodes[index] = null` via `prisma.user.update(...)`. Two concurrent authorize requests with the same `credentials.backupCode` can both pass the `index !== -1` check before either update commits, granting two sessions for a supposed single-use code (TOCTOU race). A similar check-then-update pattern exists in the disable endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`): it verifies `req.body.backupCode` against decrypted codes but does not atomically consume/lock it before the later `prisma.user.update` that clears `backupCodes`/disables 2FA, so concurrent requests can both pass verification based on the same stored value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code input not normalized (only dashes stripped) — whitespace or uppercase input fails verification with misleading error

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` in `totp/setup.ts`). Verification in both disable (`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`) and login (`credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `next-auth-options.ts`) only strips dashes and then does a case-sensitive `indexOf(...)` against stored codes. There is no `trim()` or lowercasing, so common user input variants (uppercase hex, leading/trailing whitespace or embedded spaces from copy/paste) will fail verification and return `IncorrectBackupCode` even when the underlying code matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) can throw unhandled on corrupt/rotated data, crashing the auth path with an opaque InternalServerError

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple new code paths that do `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without any try/catch or validation. In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` will throw if `user.backupCodes` is corrupted, not valid JSON, or cannot be decrypted (e.g., rotated key / bad ciphertext), resulting in an unhandled exception and a 500 response. Similarly in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` within `authorize()`, the same pattern is used for login via backup code. These exceptions are not converted into a controlled `ErrorCode`, making the auth/disable flow fail opaquely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setup endpoint overwrites existing backup codes before 2FA is confirmed, silently invalidating codes the user already saved on repeated setup calls

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup handler always generates a fresh `backupCodes` array and immediately persists it via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...), twoFactorEnabled: false, twoFactorSecret: ... } })` before 2FA is actually enabled/confirmed. Re-invoking the setup endpoint will overwrite any previously stored backup codes (including ones the user may have already saved) even if the user never completes the enable step, effectively silently invalidating them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Clipboard copy is fire-and-forget with no error handling, giving no feedback on failure and risking users believing codes were copied

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, the copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without `await`/`.then`/`.catch`, and immediately shows a success toast (`showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")`). If clipboard access is denied/unavailable (common without HTTPS/permissions), the promise can reject but the UI still reports success, misleading users into thinking codes were copied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: URL.createObjectURL blob URL never revoked on unmount, leaking the object URL

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, a blob URL is created via `setBackupCodesUrl(URL.createObjectURL(textBlob))` when setup succeeds. The code only revokes the previous URL when creating a new one (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), but there is no cleanup on modal close/unmount (`resetState()` doesn’t revoke and no `useEffect` cleanup exists). This can leak object URLs if the component unmounts or the modal is closed after generating codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No client-side double-submission guard on backup-code verification could consume a valid code on a duplicate request (verify isDisabling covers the lost-access branch)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a client-side double-submission guard in `DisableTwoFactorModal.handleDisable`: it immediately returns when `isDisabling` is true (`if (isDisabling) return;`), and the backup-code (“lost access”) flow uses the same submit handler (it only conditionally renders `<BackupCode />` vs `<TwoFactor />`). So the claim that there is *no* guard for the lost-access/backup-code branch is not supported by the diff. Also, the disable endpoint doesn’t consume an individual backup code; it disables 2FA and clears all backup codes (`backupCodes: null`) once, so a duplicate request wouldn’t “consume a valid code” beyond what a single successful disable already does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) surfaces the enum string as error message, a fragile client contract replicated in new call sites

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` usages when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing (in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`). Throwing the enum value as the Error message means downstream error handling may rely on the thrown string matching an `ErrorCode` (a client/server contract). This pattern already existed for other auth errors, but the change does replicate/extend that coupling into new code paths; whether that string is surfaced to clients depends on surrounding handlers not shown in the diff, so it’s a contract/robustness concern rather than a directly verifiable defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for the backup-code login flow in authorize() (missing key, MissingBackupCodes, IncorrectBackupCode, dash stripping, code consumption + re-encryption) at next-auth-options.ts:131-156, despite a TODO acknowledging missing tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial backup-code login logic in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (new `backupCode` credential field, decrypting `user.backupCodes`, `replaceAll("-", "")` dash stripping, error cases `MissingBackupCodes`/`IncorrectBackupCode`, and code consumption + re-encryption via `symmetricEncrypt` + `prisma.user.update`). No corresponding unit/integration tests for these branches are added anywhere in the diff. The only added test changes are Playwright checks around displaying/downloading/copying backup codes (and a TODO comment in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` explicitly noting missing backup code tests), but nothing covers the `authorize()` backup-code flow or its error cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that backup codes are single-use; replayed codes not verified as rejected, and indexOf on array with null entries is fragile to regressions like switching to delete mutations

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds single-use backup code consumption in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` by setting the matched code entry to `null` and re-encrypting the array (`backupCodes[index] = null; ... prisma.user.update(...)`). However, the added Playwright coverage only tests download/copy/close UI (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`) and even contains a TODO to add more backup code tests; it does not verify that a consumed backup code is rejected on replay. The note about `indexOf` being fragile with `null` entries is more of a forward-looking robustness concern than a currently verifiable defect, but the missing single-use test for this new nontrivial logic is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for disabling 2FA with a backup code in disable.ts:46-68 or the 'lost access' toggle UI in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior for disabling 2FA via backup code in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (new branch handling `req.body.backupCode`, errors `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes`, and clearing `backupCodes` on disable) and a new “Lost access” toggle path in `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` that switches between `<TwoFactor .../>` and `<BackupCode .../>`. The only test change shown is in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, which adds backup-code-related checks for the *enable* flow and even includes a TODO explicitly noting missing tests for “disabling 2fa with backup”. No test additions for the disable-backup-code path or the modal toggle UI are present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: E2E test verifies download/copy button clicks but not their outputs — TODO comments for checking file and clipboard content mean formatting bugs in formatBackupCode or wrong blobs would pass

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the new test steps for backup codes only click the download/copy buttons and assert the suggested filename / toast presence, but explicitly leave `// TODO: check file content` and `// TODO: check clipboard content`. Given new nontrivial logic in `EnableTwoFactorModal` (e.g., `formatBackupCode`, Blob creation, `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"))`), formatting/serialization issues could slip through while the E2E still passes. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for the new DisplayBackupCodes step gating in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135; resetState() not called when dialog closed via onOpenChange during backup-codes step (stale codes possible) and backupCodesUrl never revoked on unmount

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, state is not reset when the dialog is closed via the Dialog's `onOpenChange` (e.g., backdrop click / ESC). `resetState()` is only called from the Cancel button handler and the backup-codes Close button (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`), but `onOpenChange` is passed through without wrapping to clear `step/password/backupCodes` etc. This can leave the modal reopening in `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` with stale `backupCodes`/`backupCodesUrl`. Also, `backupCodesUrl` is only revoked when a new URL is created, not on reset/unmount, so an object URL can leak if the modal is closed after creation without another setup run. The "no test" portion is secondary, but the stale-state/URL-cleanup issues are verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for setup endpoint backup-code generation (setup.ts:60-70): code format vs UI minLength/maxLength expectations and symmetricEncrypt round-trip through the DB unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial backup-code generation and encrypted persistence in the setup endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`: generates `backupCodes` via `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, stores `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...)`, and returns them). There are UI constraints for entry (`BackupCode.tsx` `minLength={10}`, `maxLength={11}` with optional dash) and later server-side normalization (`replaceAll("-", "")` in both login authorize and disable endpoint), but the added tests only cover UI interactions (download/copy/close) and do not verify setup output format, nor that `symmetricEncrypt` data survives a DB round-trip and can be decrypted/used. This is a concrete missing-test gap for newly introduced logic, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pre-existing broken assertion at login.2fa.e2e.ts:49-51 — expect(...isChecked()).toBeTruthy() always passes because expect() of a PromiseLike is truthy; FIXME added but not fixed

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the code does `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();`. `locator.isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>`, and passing that promise directly into `expect()` makes the assertion effectively check the truthiness of the Promise object (always truthy), not the resolved boolean. The diff even adds a `FIXME` noting it "passes even when switch is not checked" without fixing it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for MissingBackupCodes / mixed-state users (existing users with backupCodes = null but twoFactorEnabled = true) — most likely production edge case

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new error paths for users with `twoFactorEnabled` but no stored `backupCodes`: login authorize throws `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` and `!user.backupCodes` (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts), and the disable endpoint returns the same error when `req.body.backupCode` is provided but `!user.backupCodes` (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts). A Prisma migration adds `backupCodes` as nullable (schema.prisma + migration), so mixed-state existing users (2FA enabled, backupCodes null) are plausible. The Playwright test only covers enabling 2FA and displaying/copying/downloading backup codes, with a TODO noting more backup code tests (apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts). No test covers the `MissingBackupCodes` scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code verification logic duplicated between next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts, with divergence: login path consumes codes while disable path does not, and error-handling styles differ; should be a shared verifyBackupCode helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated backup-code verification in two places: (1) `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` inside `authorize()` (decrypt `user.backupCodes`, `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, throw errors, and consume the matched code by re-encrypting with `backupCodes[index] = null`), and (2) `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (same decrypt/parse/index check and error codes, but it does not consume a single code and instead later clears all codes via `backupCodes: null` when disabling 2FA). This divergence is real and can be justified by differing flows, but the duplication and different error-handling patterns (throwing errors vs returning JSON error responses) are diff-grounded and support the recommendation to centralize logic in a shared helper to avoid drift.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useState([]) in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx infers never[] and breaks the type boundary; should be useState<string[]>([]) with a typed response body

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` the state is initialized as `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);`. In TypeScript, `useState([])` infers `never[]` (empty array literal), which makes later uses like `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes);` and `backupCodes.map((code) => ...)` type-incompatible and can fail compilation under typical strict TS settings. The finding’s suggested fix (`useState<string[]>([])` and typing the response body) is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resetState in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx is incomplete: doesn't clear dataUri, secret, backupCodes, or backupCodesUrl, causing stale state on modal reuse and unreleased object URLs

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, resetState() only calls setPassword(""), setErrorMessage(null), and setStep(ConfirmPassword). It does not clear dataUri, secret, backupCodes, or backupCodesUrl, even though those are set during setup (setBackupCodes, setBackupCodesUrl via URL.createObjectURL, setDataUri, setSecret). This can leave stale sensitive values in component state across modal reuse and, more concretely, can leak an object URL because backupCodesUrl is only revoked in handleSetup when generating a new one, not when cancelling/closing via resetState().

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code format (5 chars, dash, 5 chars) is hardcoded in three places (formatBackupCode, BackupCode input constraints, server strip-dash normalization) risking drift; should be a shared constant/util

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the backup-code presentation/validation rules duplicated in multiple places: UI formatting in `EnableTwoFactorModal` via `formatBackupCode = (code) => `${code.slice(0, 5)}-${code.slice(5, 10)}`; UI constraints in `BackupCode.tsx` (`placeholder="XXXXX-XXXXX"`, `minLength={10}`, `maxLength={11}`); and server-side normalization by stripping dashes (`replaceAll("-", "")`) in both `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`. This isn’t an immediate functional bug, but it’s a concrete maintainability/consistency risk (format changes would require edits in multiple locations).

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackupCode.tsx exports a component named TwoFactor while a different TwoFactor component exists in TwoFactor.tsx, causing naming confusion
matched_golden_ids: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying issue: in BackupCode.tsx the exported component/function is named TwoFactor even though it implements backup-code behavior, creating inconsistent/misleading naming (and potential confusion with a TwoFactor component in TwoFactor.tsx).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts disable() declares backupCode as required string but callers pass empty/undefined; should be optional backupCode?: string

adjudication.rationale: In TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable the new signature `disable(password: string, code: string, backupCode: string)` makes `backupCode` mandatory even though it’s only conditionally used server-side (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` in `totp/disable.ts`). In the UI, the same modal can submit via TOTP without a backup code (it conditionally renders `<TwoFactor ... />` vs `<BackupCode ... />`), so `backupCode` is effectively “not applicable” and may be `""`/unset. Making `backupCode` optional (`backupCode?: string`) would better reflect intended usage and avoid forcing meaningless values in calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/stale comments in disable.ts contradict the code structure and add comment-noise

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the added comments (e.g., "if user has 2fa and using backup code" and "if user has 2fa and NOT using backup code, try totp") match the `if/else if` structure shown and don’t contradict behavior. The complaint is essentially about comment noise/style rather than a verifiable functional issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: backupCodes array permanently contains null holes after code use, undocumented invariant that will trip maintainers; should use shared type/helper or splice instead of null-assignment

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, when a backup code is successfully used, the code does `backupCodes[index] = null;` and re-encrypts the whole array. This leaves persistent `null` entries (“holes”) in the stored JSON array, creating an implicit invariant (array of strings-or-nulls) that other code must tolerate. While current checks use `indexOf(...)` (so `null` entries don’t immediately break correctness), it’s a maintainability concern and could surprise future code that assumes `string[]` (e.g., iterating/displaying/counting remaining codes). Using a shared helper/type or removing the element (e.g., splice/filter) would avoid that hidden invariant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lost-access toggle state machine duplicated between login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx with subtly differing reset helpers; should be extracted into a shared component

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces very similar “lost access” toggle logic in two places: `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` uses `twoFactorLostAccess` to switch between `<TwoFactor>` and `<BackupCode>` and manually resets different fields in the footer handler (`methods.setValue("totpCode", "")` vs `methods.setValue("backupCode", "")`, plus `setErrorMessage(null)`). `apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` adds a parallel `twoFactorLostAccess` toggle with its own `resetForm(clearPassword = true)` helper and different reset semantics (`resetForm(false)` when toggling to preserve password, but clears codes and error). This is a concrete duplication/architecture concern introduced by the change (risk of diverging behavior), not a direct functional defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is consumed inside authorize() before the session is guaranteed; if sign-in fails after authorize succeeds, the code is burned with no session issued

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` the code is immediately invalidated by updating the DB (`backupCodes[index] = null; await prisma.user.update(...)`) inside `authorize()`. The diff does not show any transaction or guarantee that a session/JWT is successfully issued after `authorize()` returns, so a downstream failure after `authorize()` (e.g., later NextAuth callbacks/response errors) could burn a one-time backup code without the user being logged in.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic verify-then-consume of backup code allows the same code to be used by two concurrent login requests

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup codes are validated by decrypting `user.backupCodes`, finding the index, then updating the DB in a separate `prisma.user.update` call (`const index = backupCodes.indexOf(...)` then `backupCodes[index] = null; await prisma.user.update(...)`). There is no transaction/conditional update tying the check to the consume, so two concurrent login requests can both read the same encrypted list, both find the code present, and both succeed before either update is persisted—allowing double-use of a “single-use” backup code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disable endpoint calls JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) with no validation, causing unhandled exception and raw 500 on malformed ciphertext

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode`, the handler does `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));` with no try/catch or validation. If `user.backupCodes` is corrupted/malformed (decrypt fails or yields non-JSON), `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` will throw and the request will result in an unhandled exception and a 500 response rather than a controlled error. This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 'All codes used' state is indistinguishable from 'codes exist' because used codes are replaced with null inside an encrypted array that stays truthy, yielding IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes and never clearing the column

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup codes are stored as an encrypted JSON array (`user.backupCodes` truthy if column is non-null). When a backup code is used, the code sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts the array, but does not remove nulls or clear the column when all are consumed. On subsequent logins, `if (!user.backupCodes)` will not trigger, and `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` will return `-1` (since the array contains `null`s), causing `IncorrectBackupCode` rather than `MissingBackupCodes`. There is also no code path here that nulls `backupCodes` once all are used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setup endpoint regenerates and overwrites backupCodes on every call, silently invalidating previously shown codes and persisting codes even if 2FA is never enabled

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, each setup request generates a fresh `backupCodes` array (`crypto.randomBytes...`) and immediately persists it via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...), twoFactorEnabled: false, ... }})`. This overwrites any previously generated/stored backup codes on every call to the setup endpoint, invalidating codes a user may have already been shown/saved. It also stores backup codes (and a new secret) even though `twoFactorEnabled` remains `false`, so codes are persisted even if the user cancels before completing 2FA enablement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EnableTwoFactorModal doesn't call resetState() when the dialog is dismissed via overlay/X, leaving stale state and the password buffer in memory

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, state like `password`, `step`, `backupCodesUrl`, etc. is stored in React state and only cleared via `resetState()` on explicit button handlers (Cancel button click and the Backup Codes “close” button). The dialog is controlled by `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>`, but there is no effect or wrapper that calls `resetState()` when `onOpenChange(false)` occurs (e.g., dismiss via overlay click or X/close control). If the Dialog does not unmount the modal content when closed (common for controlled dialogs), reopening can retain the previous `step` and keep the `password` value in memory/UI, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Object URL leak in EnableTwoFactorModal: the final URL is never revoked on unmount

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, a Blob Object URL is created via `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` and stored in `backupCodesUrl`. The code only revokes the *previous* URL when creating a new one (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), but there is no cleanup on modal close/reset/unmount. `resetState()` does not revoke the current `backupCodesUrl`, and the cancel/close handlers call `resetState()` and return without `URL.revokeObjectURL(...)`. If the component is reopened or unmounted, the final Object URL can remain allocated, causing a resource leak.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No down/rollback script provided for the migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a Prisma migration file `packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql` containing only an `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`. Prisma migrations in this repo appear to be forward-only SQL files (no separate down/rollback script mechanism shown anywhere in the diff), so calling out a “missing down/rollback script” is not a verifiable defect or even a clearly applicable review issue based on what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fragile client/server format coupling: client enforces backup code shape only via bypassable HTML attributes, and server does no length/format validation or canonicalization (e.g., stripping trailing whitespace)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code auth paths that only canonicalize by stripping dashes (`replaceAll("-", "")`) in both login authorize and the disable API, but do not trim whitespace or normalize case before lookup. See `disable.ts`: `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` and `next-auth-options.ts`: `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`. The client `BackupCode` component only sets `minLength`/`maxLength` and a placeholder, which is bypassable and doesn’t prevent common paste issues (trailing newline/space) or uppercase hex input; those will cause false `IncorrectBackupCode` errors even for valid codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Login form's zod resolver schema may not include backupCode, so the field could be stripped before submission if it's a strict zod object

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` the form uses `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })` and the new UI registers a `backupCode` field (`<BackupCode ... />` uses `methods.register("backupCode")`). The diff adds `backupCode` to `LoginValues` and toggling logic sets/clears it, but there is no corresponding change shown to `formSchema` to include `backupCode`. With Zod, unknown keys are typically stripped during parsing, so `backupCode` may be dropped from the submitted values and never reach `next-auth` (which now expects `credentials.backupCode`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race condition: backup code redemption (read → indexOf → write) is not atomic, allowing a single-use code to be consumed twice under concurrent requests in next-auth-options.ts

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login does a non-atomic read/modify/write: it decrypts `user.backupCodes`, finds the code via `indexOf`, then updates the row with a modified/encrypted array (`backupCodes[index] = null` followed by `prisma.user.update`). There is no transaction/locking/conditional update ensuring the code was unused at write time, so two concurrent requests using the same backup code could both pass the `indexOf` check before either write occurs, allowing a supposedly single-use code to be redeemed twice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing 2FA users have backupCodes = null with no migration, backfill, or regenerate endpoint, silently locking them out of backup code recovery

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nullable `backupCodes` column (Prisma + migration) and logic that depends on it for backup-code login/disable. Backup codes are only generated in the 2FA setup endpoint (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`) and shown after enabling 2FA, but there’s no backfill/migration logic or any regenerate endpoint/UI for users who already had `twoFactorEnabled=true` before this change. Those users will have `backupCodes = null` and hit `MissingBackupCodes` (e.g., in `next-auth-options.ts` and `totp/disable.ts`) if they try the new “lost access” backup-code path. This doesn’t break normal TOTP-based 2FA login, and it isn’t “silent” (it returns a specific error), but it is a real completeness/rollout gap created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setup.ts persists/overwrites backup codes before TOTP is actually enabled and on every call, silently destroying previously issued codes if the flow is abandoned or repeated

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup endpoint now generates `backupCodes` and immediately persists them via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: ... , twoFactorEnabled: false, twoFactorSecret: ... }})` on every call, before 2FA is actually enabled. This overwrites any previously stored `user.backupCodes` each time setup is retried/abandoned/repeated, invalidating previously issued codes without any explicit regeneration step or user confirmation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setup endpoint returns backup codes in the JSON response at a point where 2FA is not yet enabled, leaking valid persisted credentials on aborted setups

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` now generates backup codes, persists them to the user record, and returns them in the JSON response while `twoFactorEnabled` is explicitly left `false` (setup.ts: generates `backupCodes`, stores `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...)`, and returns `{ secret, keyUri, dataUri, backupCodes }`). That’s a real flow/design concern (backup codes exist and are exposed to the client before 2FA is actually enabled), but the finding’s framing as a “leak” of “valid persisted credentials” on aborted setups is not fully verifiable from the diff because the response goes to the authenticated caller and those codes are not accepted for login/disable unless `user.twoFactorEnabled` is true (next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts both gate backup-code use on `twoFactorEnabled`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code comparison uses indexOf (not constant-time), codes are only 40 bits with no per-code attempt lockout, and codes are encrypted but not hashed so a key leak exposes all codes in plaintext

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup codes generated as `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` (10 hex chars = 40 bits) in `totp/setup.ts`, stored via `symmetricEncrypt(...)` (not hashed), and later checked using `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` in both `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`. This makes the comparison non-constant-time and means compromise of `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` would expose all backup codes in plaintext. The diff does not show any specific per-code attempt lockout/rate limiting around these checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY throws a raw Error in disable.ts bypassing the JSON error contract, and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throws raw on corrupt data

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path does `if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) { ... throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError); }`, which will bypass the endpoint’s normal `res.status(...).json({ error })` contract and likely surface as an unhandled 500/non-contract response. Also, `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` is not guarded; if decryption fails or the decrypted value is not valid JSON, it will throw a raw exception and similarly bypass the JSON error response contract. Both behaviors are directly introduced by this diff in the new backup code handling block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dismissing the enable modal via X/overlay/Esc after enabling never calls onEnable, leaving parent switch state stale and resuming at a stale step with stale backupCodes

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, successful enable no longer calls onEnable; it only does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` (handleEnable success). `onEnable()` is only invoked by the explicit “close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes step. However the Dialog can also be dismissed via X/overlay/Esc through `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` without any wrapper calling `onEnable()` or even `resetState()`. That means after enabling, dismissing via overlay/Esc will not notify the parent (switch can remain stale) and component state like `step`/`backupCodes` can remain at DisplayBackupCodes with previous codes when reopened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setting backupCodes[index] = null mixes 'never issued' and 'used' states, poisoning future indexOf semantics; deleting the element or tracking a used-set would be safer

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, after a successful match (`const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));`), the code sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts the array. This does not break `indexOf` for future lookups: `indexOf(<string>)` will simply skip `null` entries, so used codes cannot be reused while unused string codes remain matchable. The diff does not show any separate “never issued” state that would be conflated with `null`, nor any logic that depends on array indexes beyond lookup, so the claimed “poisoning future indexOf semantics” is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code acceptance is case/whitespace sensitive with no server-side normalization (only '-' is stripped), so uppercase or whitespace-padded input fails

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex strings in `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`), but both verification paths only strip dashes and do no other normalization: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`. There is no `trim()` or lowercasing, so leading/trailing whitespace or uppercased input (placeholder shows `XXXXX-XXXXX`) will fail lookup against stored lowercase codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: E2E assertion expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() is a no-op because isChecked() returns a Promise, so the enabled state is unverified

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the test does `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();`. `locator.isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>`, so `expect(<Promise>).toBeTruthy()` asserts the promise object (always truthy) rather than the resolved boolean. This means the enabled/checked state is not actually verified, matching the finding (and is even hinted by the added `// FIXME` comment).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is consumed via prisma.user.update inside authorize before next-auth completes sign-in, so any downstream session-creation failure burns the code

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` is true, the code is immediately “consumed” by mutating the stored backup codes (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and persisting via `await prisma.user.update(...)` inside `authorize(...)` before NextAuth finishes the rest of the sign-in flow. If anything after `authorize` fails (e.g., session/JWT/callback handling), the user would not be signed in but the backup code would already be invalidated, effectively burning a one-time code without a successful login.
